monthly_review.summary: You've increased running intensity and efficiency this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — reflected in faster paces, elevated HR, and improved aerobic TE and cadence despite slightly lower total km.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved by +0.37 m/sec per bpm — the largest positive shift across all metrics — indicating better cardiovascular economy at given intensities.

goal_tracker.message: You need 5.1 more km across 2 remaining sessions to match last month's volume — e.g., two 2.6–3.0 km runs, ideally one with Zone 2 focus and one with Zone 3 tempo segments.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.79 m/sec per bpm while average HR increased +4 bpm — confirming improved oxygen utilization per heartbeat, likely driven by recent Zone 3/4 work (25% and 15% of time this month vs 19% and 3% last month).

insights.title: Shift toward threshold and VO2 max stimulus
insights.body: Zone 3+ time jumped from 22% (Z3:19%, Z4:3%, Z5:0%) last month to 42% (Z3:25%, Z4:15%, Z5:2%) this month — a meaningful increase in high-aerobic stress that explains pace gains but may require monitoring for fatigue.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff under speed
insights.body: On your fastest recent run (2026-06-11, 6:32 min/km), cadence spiked to 162 spm and stride length jumped to 91.13 cm — unusually high for your typical ~69–71 cm — suggesting form adaptation to speed, but vertical oscillation also rose to 8.4 cm (+0.7 cm above monthly avg), possibly increasing energy cost.

insights.title: Low-HR recovery run underutilized
insights.body: Only 1 of 5 recent runs (2026-06-19, HR=112 bpm) was truly in Zone 1 (<120 bpm); your other easy runs averaged 137–144 bpm — meaning most 'easy' efforts are drifting into Zone 2 or low Zone 3, reducing recovery benefit.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5 km Zone 1 effort (HR ≤ 120 bpm), using your 2026-06-19 run (HR=112 bpm) as pacing reference — walk if needed to stay below 120 bpm.
recommendations.reason: Only 27% of this month’s time was spent in Zone 1, and your most recent true recovery run shows you can reliably hit Zone 1; rebuilding this capacity supports sustainable Zone 3/4 work.

recommendations.action: Add 2x 3-minute Zone 3 intervals (HR 150–158 bpm) at 4:45–5:00 min/km pace during your next 8 km run, with 3-min Zone 1 jog recoveries.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 3 time increased this month but remains unstructured — these intervals target lactate threshold development while respecting your current VO2 max estimate (37–38 mL/kg/min) and recent 3.2 km pace capability.

recommendations.action: After any run with cadence ≥ 160 spm (e.g., like 2026-06-11), perform 3×1 min barefoot strides on grass focusing on landing quietly and minimizing vertical oscillation (target <7.5 cm).
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation rose to 8.4 cm on your highest-cadence run — a 10% increase over your monthly average (7.7 cm) — suggesting neuromuscular inefficiency at speed that can be addressed with targeted drill work.

weekly_focus.description: Balance the recent uptick in Zone 3/4 work with deliberate low-HR recovery and controlled threshold stimulus — reinforcing aerobic resilience without accumulating fatigue.
suggested_sessions: 3 km easy + 3×1 min barefoot grass strides
